local cl_fov_enabled = CreateClientConVar("cl_fov_enabled", 1, true, false, "Enable custom FOV?")
local running = false

local function CalcView(ply, pos, angles, fov, ...)
    if running or ply:GetVehicle():GetThirdPersonMode() or IsValid(ply:GetObserverTarget()) or (IsValid(ply:GetActiveWeapon()) and ply:GetActiveWeapon():GetClass() == "gmod_camera") then

    end

    local newFOV = math.Remap(fov, MinVanillaFOV, cl_fov_desired:GetInt(), MinVanillaFOV, cl_fov_desired:GetInt())
    local t = hook.Run("CalcView", ply, pos, angles, newFOV, ...) or { origin = pos, fov = newFOV }

    running = false

    return t
end

local function ToggleFOVRemap()
    if cl_fov_enabled:GetBool() then
        hook.Add("CalcView", "FOVRemap.CalcView", CalcView)
    else
        hook.Remove("CalcView", "FOVRemap.CalcView")

end

Background: Following is some material on advanced design patterns in RESTful API and microservice architecture:
- Idempotency key: sometimes we want to ensure certain actions are performed at most once. The idempotency key pattern implement this by having the client supply a client-generated key and add it as part of their request. Server side should ensure that subsequent repeated requests with the same idempotency key is ignored or that its effect is idempotent - that doing the action twice or more is the same as doing it just once.
- Other metadata: a RESTful API endpoint could allow the client to add its own metadata object in the request, with arbitrary json data allowed as long as its top level is an object.
- Controller resource: A common question in REST is how can complex transaction be modelled if REST is mostly like plain CRUD on data. One pattern to solve for this is to explicitly model such a transaction/operation as an abstract object itself, with lifecycle controlled/triggered by doing RESTful operation on this resources.
- Distributed Saga and Compensating transaction: on the backend, a business transaction may correspond to multiple DB transaction, and potentially involve external/3rd party API calls. These are all actions that fundamentally cannot be made ACID. These pattern solve this problem by using an alternative model where each step is made idempotent, with explicit procedure to compensate for the effect through a separate action in the event the whole business transaction is considered to have failed and need to be "rollbacked" (note the quote because it is not rollback in the conventional sense).

Narrative reviews, commentaries, editorials and articles published in languages other than English and French were excluded. Study quality and risk of bias were assessed using the National Institutes of Health Quality assessment tool and the revised Cochrane risk‐of‐bias tool. Results are reported according to PRISMA guidelines.    Results  Of 724 records screened, three studies met the criteria: two trials conducted in Kenya and a retrospective cohort study conducted in Cambodia. All studies reported improvement in BP control after 12 months follow‐up with reductions in systolic BP of 23, 14.8, and 16.9 mmHg, respectively. Two studies reported diabetes parameters. The harvesting chains work the same way for the egg resource.

Harvesting an egg cell will spawn as many ants as resources havested. The ants will spawn on the player’s base on the start of next turn. In games with multiple bases per player, the extra ants will spawn on each base, regardless of the base present in the harvest chain.

Harvesting is calculated separately for each resource, and for each one the game will automatically choose the best chain from its cell to your base.

Attack Chains
A player’s harvest chains may be broken by their opponent’s attack chains.

When computing harvest chains, some cells may have ants from both players. For each of these cells, the attack chain of both players is computed, and if one of the player has a lower value, this cell cannot be counted in the harvest chain.

The attack chain value for a given cell is the weakest link in a chain from that cell to one of the player’s bases.

Actions

LINE index1 index2 strength: place beacons all along a path from index1 to index2, all of strength strength. A shortest path is chosen automatically.
WAIT: do nothing.

Question: What are principal rotations, and how can any spatial rotation be decomposed into them?

Answer: Principal rotations are rotations around the three axes of a coordinate system: the x, y, and z axes. Any rotation in three-dimensional space can be decomposed into a combination of these principal rotations. To perform a rotation around a point or axis in three-dimensional space, you can first rotate around the x axis, then rotate around the y axis, and finally rotate around the z axis. This is known as the "axis-angle" representation of a rotation. In two dimensions, the principal rotations are around the x and y axes, and a rotation can be decomposed into a combination of these two. Principal rotations form a group under the operation of composition, meaning that if you perform one rotation followed by another, the result is also a rotation.

Genau bei diesem Gedanken setzt der neue Roman von Juli Zeh an. 1. Rapid Development: Tailwind CSS allows for quick development by providing ready-to-use utility classes, eliminating the need to write custom CSS code from scratch.

2. Consistency: Tailwind CSS promotes a consistent design language across projects with a predefined set of styles, ensuring a cohesive and unified look and feel.

3. Scalability: As projects grow in complexity, Tailwind CSS simplifies design maintenance and modifications by allowing developers to add or remove classes without breaking the existing code.

4. Accessibility: Tailwind CSS includes built-in accessibility features, such as proper hierarchy and ARIA attributes, making it easier to create accessible designs without additional code.

5. Customizability: Tailwind CSS is highly customizable, allowing developers to tailor the framework to fit their specific design requirements and create unique styles.

6. Community Support: With a large and active community, Tailwind CSS offers abundant resources, documentation, and community support, making it easier to learn and get help when needed.

In summary, Tailwind CSS saves development time, ensures consistency, enables scalability, enhances accessibility, provides customizability, and offers strong community support. Observe the dog’s behavior: Look at the dog’s body language to try to determine its mood and intentions. Is the dog aggressive or timid? Does it have a collar or tag? Try to speak to the dog softly and slowly to see if you can get a response.
Contact local authorities: Call your local animal control office or police department to report the incident. They will likely send someone out to help you safely capture the dog and return it to its owner. You can also contact a nearby animal shelter or rescue organization for assistance.
Provide water and food: Offer the dog fresh water and food if they seem hungry or thirsty. This may help to keep them calm while you wait for help to arrive. However, avoid approaching the dog too closely or trying to touch them unless you know they are friendly.
Be patient and cautious: Remember that the dog may be scared or confused, and their behavior may be unpredictable. Stay alert and be ready to act quickly if necessary. If the dog becomes aggressive or tries to bite you, call for help immediately.

import random

def generate_key_pair(address_database):
    while True:
        # Generate a private key (44-bit entropy)
        entropy = random.getrandbits(44)
        private_key = hashlib.sha256(str(hashlib.sha256(str(entropy).encode()).hexdigest()).encode()).hexdigest()

        # Generate a public key from the private key
        sk = ecdsa.SigningKey.from_string(bytes.fromhex(private_key), curve=ecdsa.SECP256k1)
        vk = sk.get_verifying_key()

        # Generate the uncompressed public key
        public_key_uncompressed = '04' + vk.to_string().hex()

        # Generate the Bitcoin address from the uncompressed public key
        ripemd160 = hashlib.new('ripemd160')
        ripemd160.update(hashlib.sha256(bytes.fromhex(public_key_uncompressed)).digest())
        hashed_public_key = b"\x00" + ripemd160.digest()
        checksum = hashlib.sha256(hashlib.sha256(hashed_public_key).digest()).digest()[:4]
        bitcoin_address_uncompressed = base58.b58encode(hashed_public_key + checksum).decode()

        # Generate the compressed public key
        public_key_point = vk.pubkey.point
        x = public_key_point.x()
        y = public_key_point.y()
        if y % 2 == 0:
            public_key_compressed = '02' + format(x, '064x')
        else:
            public_key_compressed = '03' + format(x, '064x')

        # Generate the Bitcoin address from the compressed public key
        ripemd160_compressed = hashlib.new('ripemd160')
        ripemd160_compressed.update(hashlib.sha256(bytes.fromhex(public_key_compressed)).digest())
        hashed_public_key_compressed = b"\x00" + ripemd160_compressed.digest()
        checksum_compressed = hashlib.sha256(hashlib.sha256(hashed_public_key_compressed).digest()).digest()[:4]
        bitcoin_address_compressed = base58.b58encode(hashed_public_key_compressed + checksum_compressed).decode()

        # Check if the generated address matches the database
        if bitcoin_address_uncompressed in address_database or bitcoin_address_compressed in address_database:
            return bitcoin_address_uncompressed, bitcoin_address_compressed, private_key, entropy

Die gesetzliche Grundlage in Deutschland ergibt sich aus § 44 Abs. 5 i. V. m. § 15 Bundesnaturschutzgesetz (Eingriffsregelung). CEF-Maßnahmen setzen direkt am betroffenen Bestand der geschützten Arten an. Sie sollen die Lebensstätte (Habitat) für die betroffene Population in Qualität und Quantität erhalten. Die Maßnahme soll dabei einen unmittelbaren räumlichen Bezug zum betroffenen Habitat haben und angrenzend neue Lebensräume schaffen, die in direkter funktionaler Beziehung mit dem Ursprungshabitat stehen.

"Документ:
Искусственный интеллект - это область науки и технологии, которая занимается созданием компьютерных программ и машин, способных производить интеллектуальные действия, которые обычно ассоциируются с людьми, такие как обучение, анализ данных, распознавание речи и обработка естественного языка. Некоторые из наиболее популярных применений искусственного интеллекта включают в себя: автопилоты самолетов, роботы-пылесосы, голосовые помощники, системы рекомендаций, автоматизированные транспортные системы и многое другое.

Одним из наиболее известных подходов к созданию искусственного интеллекта является машинное обучение. Это метод обработки данных, который позволяет компьютеру находить образцы в данных и использовать их для обучения. Машинное обучение включает в себя различные методы, такие как нейронные сети, метод опорных векторов, деревья решений и многое другое. Однако, в последнее время, с развитием глубокого обучения, нейронные сети стали основным методом машинного обучения.

Глубокое обучение - это подход к машинному обучению, который использует многократно сверточные нейронные сети для анализа данных. Он позволяет компьютеру "обучаться" на основе большого количества данных и создавать модели, которые могут делать прогнозы и классифицировать данные с высокой точностью. In this paper, we tackle the problem of detecting samples that are not drawn from the training distribution, i.e., out-of-distribution (OOD) samples, in classification. Many previous studies have attempted to solve this problem by regarding samples with low classification confidence as OOD examples using deep neural networks (DNNs). However, on difficult datasets or models with low classification ability, these methods incorrectly regard in-distribution samples close to the decision boundary as OOD samples. This problem arises because their approaches use only the features close to the output layer and disregard the uncertainty of the features. Therefore, we propose a method that extracts the uncertainties of features in each layer of DNNs using a reparameterization trick and combines them. In experiments, our method outperforms the existing methods by a large margin, achieving state-of-the-art detection performance on several datasets and classification models. For example, our method increases the AUROC score of prior work (83.8%) to 99.8% in DenseNet on the CIFAR-100 and Tiny-ImageNet datasets.

After proving the transcriptomic similarity of sister cells at stages I and II (Figures S4AS4D), we quantitatively analyzed the lineage relationships between different cross-stage cell-type pairs by potential-spective or origin-spective analyses and identiﬁed many previously uncharacterized converging or diverging trajectories (Figures 3C, 3D, and S3D–S3G). For diverging trajectories, we found that NP pHB and NP MHB had multilineage fates from stages I to II or stages II to III. The NP pHB in stage I (I-NPpHB ) could differentiate into II-NPpHB , Motors, and Seros at stage II, and II-NP pHB produced progenies with more diverging fates including NPpHB , Gluts, Motors, Seros, and GABAs at stage III (Figures 3C, 3D, and S4E). The NP MHB at stage I (I-NPMHB ) could differentiate into II-NP MHB and Gluts at stage II, and II-NP MHB could give rise to III-NP aHB and III-NP vMB at stage III (Figures 3C and 3D). For instance, NP vMB were unipotent and speciﬁcally differentiated into later-stage NP vMB from differentiation stages I to III (Figures 3C and 3D). Comment on areas of application: QLoRA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs. We present QLoRA, an efficient finetuning approach that reduces memory usage enough to finetune a 65B parameter model on a single 48GB GPU while preserving full 16-bit finetuning task performance. QLoRA backpropagates gradients through a frozen, 4-bit quantized pretrained language model into Low Rank Adapters~(LoRA). Our best model family, which we name Guanaco, outperforms all previous openly released models on the Vicuna benchmark, reaching 99.3% of the performance level of ChatGPT while only requiring 24 hours of finetuning on a single GPU. QLoRA introduces a number of innovations to save memory without sacrificing performance: (a) 4-bit NormalFloat (NF4), a new data type that is information theoretically optimal for normally distributed weights (b) double quantization to reduce the average memory footprint by quantizing the quantization constants, and (c) paged optimziers to manage memory spikes.
